findings.consequence: Pallet jams at the entry conveyor photo-eye will not be detected. The conveyor motor Y10 will continue running against the jam, causing mechanical damage to equipment, conveyor belt wear, or damage to battery packs.
findings.evidence: Conveyor entry photo-eye PE-1002 (X11) is never used in the program (confirmed by lint L005). Parameter jam_time (5.0 s on T10) and cause-effect CE-ST10-03 specify stopping the conveyor and raising a jam alarm if PE-1002 remains blocked for 5.0 s while running. M190 is reset in R2 and read in R3, but is never set anywhere.
findings.proposed_fix: Add jam detection rungs before R2: run timer T10 when conveyor runs with entry eye blocked (LD Y10 -> AND X11 -> OUT T10 K50). When T10 finishes, latch jam alarm M190 (LD T10 -> SET M190).
findings.title: Missing conveyor jam detection logic (PE-1002, T10, M190)

findings.consequence: When the thermal overload cools down and its contact recloses (X13 returns high), M191 and M199 clear automatically. If auto mode switch X2 is active, conveyor motor Y10 will immediately restart without operator intervention or pressing fault reset PB-0002.
findings.evidence: R1 drives M191 with an unlatched OUT coil based on LDI X13. R2 only resets M190 and does not reset M191. Narrative section 4.8 specifies that alarms are latched and cleared by fault reset once their cause has cleared.
findings.proposed_fix: Latch the overload alarm with SET M191 on LDI X13 in R1, and add RST M191 to R2 when fault reset pushbutton X1 is pressed.
findings.title: Motor overload alarm M191 unlatched allowing automatic restart

findings.consequence: Resetting the E-stop circuit causes immediate automatic restart of the conveyor motor without an operator pressing fault reset or initiating a start sequence, creating a safety hazard for personnel near the conveyor.
findings.evidence: In R3, ORI X0 is combined into M199, which directly enables Y10 in R4 via ANI M199. When the E-stop circuit is restored (X0 transitions from 0 to 1), M199 immediately clears. If selector switch SS-0003 (X2) is in Auto, Y10 restarts instantly.
findings.proposed_fix: Require an operator reset or start action to clear the stop condition after an E-stop event rather than automatically re-enabling M199 and Y10 solely on X0 going high.
findings.title: Automatic conveyor motor restart on E-stop circuit restoration

findings.consequence: A pulse on X14 from the line controller while the cell is in manual mode, faulted, or in an E-stop condition will drop the stopper solenoid for 2.0 s, potentially releasing pallets into an unsafe or unready station.
findings.evidence: R6 triggers SET Y11 purely on rising edge of release request RQ-1005 (LDP X14). It contains no interlock checking whether the station is in Auto mode (X2), healthy E-stop (X0), or free of active faults (ANI M199).
findings.proposed_fix: Add interlocks to R6: AND X2 (auto mode), AND X0 (E-stop healthy), and ANI M199 (no fault) before executing SET Y11. Additionally ensure Y11 is reset if E-stop is lost.
findings.title: Stopper release solenoid Y11 lacks operational and safety interlocks

data.summary: ST10 review identified four significant logic defects: missing jam detection logic (unreferenced input X11, missing timer T10, and unassigned alarm bit M190), unlatched motor overload alarm M191 causing unexpected automatic restarts upon thermal reset, unsafe automatic motor re-start when E-stop healthy contact X0 is restored while Auto mode is selected, and lack of mode and safety interlocks on stopper release solenoid Y11.
